summary: Bulk asset-return CSV triggered mass badge deprovision cascade; staging dock locked and return shipments on hold
facilities_location: London Warehouse - Dock B / Staging Room 3
description:
Issue summary:
A bulk asset-return import (CSV) into Inventory Service marked ~120 devices as 'returned' and triggered an automated deprovisioning workflow that inadvertently removed badge access for 18 active staff and locked the staging dock gate (Dock B). Several outbound vendor couriers were held because scanning the associated shipment manifest flagged assets as 'already returned'.

Impact:
- 18 staff unable to access Dock B or Staging Room 3 for morning shift (affects on-site engineer team and courier handling).
- 6 outbound shipments (GPUs, monitors, SSDs) placed on hold pending manual verification; SLA for same-day pickup at risk.
- Temporary inability to accept incoming returns that require manual staging.

Timeline (local time):
- 08:12: CSV import started by ops-tech (automated job).
- 08:18: Inventory Service completed import; deprovision job enqueued.
- 08:22: First badge access failures reported by morning team in #facilities.
- 08:35: Staging dock gate automatically entered locked state when badge validation returned null for badge mappings.
- 08:50: This ticket created and pager escalated to Facilities and Infra.

Environment:
- Inventory Service v3.5.1 (prod, EU region).
- Access-Control lambda (badge-sync) v2.2.0.
- Warehouse gate controller (vendor: SecureGate) API v1.9.

Steps to reproduce (suspected):
1) Reproduce locally by importing a CSV with mixed 'returned' statuses and missing badge_id fields into Inventory staging endpoint.
2) Ensure badge-sync job runs with 'cascade_deprovision=true' flag.
3) Observe badge records removed and gate controller receiving empty badge mapping payload.

Logs / evidence:
- Inventory import audit: https://logs.redwood.example.com/q/INV/2026-03-12/imp-2789 (CSV checksum: 9f3a1e)
- Badge-sync run (08:19): https://logs.redwood.example.com/q/AC/2026-03-12/sync-4471
- Gate controller alert: SecureGate event 0x7f3b: null badge handlers
- Slack thread: #facilities (link: https://slack.redwood.example.com/archives/C06FACIL/threads/1612)

Initial investigation notes:
- Preliminary root cause hypothesis: import CSV contained rows for assets that were already soft-returned but had badge association nullified in the CSV; the deprovision workflow did not validate active_user assignment before removing badges (regression introduced by infra PR 9705).
- Badge-sync currently treats missing badge_id as an instruction to remove mapping rather than skip. This is a policy change introduced in v2.2.0.
- Gate controller treats absence of mapping for a user badge as 'user unauthorized' and flips to lockdown when multiple invalid scans occur within 60 seconds (safety fallback).

Temporary workaround applied:
- Rolled back badge-sync to v2.1.8 at 09:05 which prevents cascade removal.
- Manually re-enabled badge mappings from snapshot backup (inventory snapshot taken 2026-03-12T07:50Z) for 18 affected staff at 09:22.
- Gate controller manually reset by on-site vendor tech at 09:40; dock unlocked and courier pickups resumed at 09:55.
- Placed affected outbound shipments on manual verification list and notified carriers; all pickups rescheduled to same day where possible.

Immediate next steps / owner actions:
- Marcus Reed (Facilities) to coordinate vendor gate health check and confirm SecureGate firmware logs for 08:22-08:40 window.
- Priya Nair (Infra) to open PR reverting the cascade behavior and add validation to inventory import pipeline to skip rows with null badge_id for active-users (tracking PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/9812).
- Inventory team to add an import preview and dry-run step to prevent accidental bulk deprovision.
- Ops to run an audit of all 'returned' status changes in last 72 hours and confirm there are no further impacted users.

Acceptance criteria for resolution:
- Badge-sync prevents removal of active user badge mappings when CSV row omits badge_id.
- Gate controller no longer enters full-lockdown from transient multi-scan null-mapping events (fail-safe changed to log + notify).
- Post-mortem with runbook updates published in Confluence and shared in #facilities.
